applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No standalone Cayman Islands bilateral investment treaty is in force; investor protection is framed by the constitutional relationship with the United Kingdom, UK bi-lateral commitments extended by Order in Council, OECD/G20 inclusive framework participation, and tax co-operation arrangements such as the UK-Cayman Tax Information Exchange Agreement of 2010.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against, at minimum: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; UK HM Treasury Sanctions List; Cayman Islands Financial Services (Sanctions) law designations; FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions List; and domestic adverse-media and PEP databases. Any exact or fuzzy PEP/sanctions hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and escalation to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer; confirmed matches result in automatic rejection of the relationship. Reinforced screening is required every three months and upon any material transaction anomaly. All records must be preserved for at least five years from the end of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry - Companies Registry Online Portal (caymanregistry.gov.ky)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal names must be in English or a direct Romanized transliteration using the Latin script. Chinese characters or other non-Latin scripts are not accepted as the registered legal name. The name must contain a permitted corporate designator such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'LLC', or an approved exempted-company suffix. The Registrar will reject names that are offensive, deceptive, confidential, or for which the proposed entity cannot lawfully carry on the indicated business under Cayman law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name clearance rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar within 14 days, together with comparative evidence of existing registrations and legal argument addressing the Registrar's stated basis for refusal. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may petition the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands by way of judicial review. In parallel, the applicant may file a fresh name-clearance application with alternative names. A reserved name that expires may be re-reserved through a new application unless another applicant has in the interim secured the same name; Registrar extensions are discretionary upon demonstration of active incorporation steps in progress.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in the Cayman Islands is mandatory; a digital mailbox or remote/virtual office alone cannot satisfy the statutory service-of-process requirement. However, the operational business of an AI LLM API platform may be conducted entirely from outside the Cayman Islands, and the same physical registered office may be provided by a licensed corporate services provider alongside resident director and secretary facilities. The entity should nevertheless assess Cayman Economic Substance Law filing obligations because activities involving the trading of intangible property or IP-derived income may require economic substance reporting even where day-to-day operations are cloud-based and offshore.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; annualized risk is estimated below 5% for a standard-risk exempted company with no regulated financial activities and no PEP/sanctions red flags. The likelihood increases materially, potentially to 15-25% within 12 months, where there is a suspicious transaction, non-compliant BO filing, inconsistent substance reporting, or payment via cryptocurrency rails subject to enhanced scrutiny.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2024 Revision), ss. 9, 10, 35, 53; Tax Concessions Act, s. 6 (exempted company status)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Cayman Islands (a British Overseas Territory under United Kingdom sovereignty)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (combined form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account required; exempted company must maintain a registered office in the Cayman Islands.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of Companies be and are hereby adopted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at [Address], Grand Cayman, and that [Registered Office Provider] be appointed as registered office provider. RESOLVED, that [Name 1] and [Name 2] be appointed as first directors, and [Name 3] as corporate secretary. RESOLVED, that subscriptions for ordinary shares reflected in the initial register be accepted. RESOLVED, that directors be authorized to apply for tax exemption status under the Tax Concessions Act. RESOLVED, that any additional approvals for AI software activities be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry – Corporate Name Database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed exempted company name via a licensed corporate service provider or the General Registry’s online filing portal. Verify against the register of companies for identical or confusingly similar names. Pay the name-check fee and obtain the name clearance certificate before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing if foreign-language name is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file an administrative objection with supporting trademark or priority evidence, or select an alternate name and resubmit the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association conforming to the Companies Act. Deliver two certified copies through an approved corporate service provider. Pay the incorporation fee (approximately USD 793). Receive the Certificate of Incorporation once the Registrar completes statutory review.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requests corrections, file amended Memorandum and Articles within 21 days without re-stamping. If the deadline lapses, apply for reinstatement under the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registered Office Provider / Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed corporate services provider to maintain a registered office in the Cayman Islands. File the registered office address and corporate secretary details with the Registrar. Update the statutory register to confirm the official contact point.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office provider declines service, execute a new provider agreement and file an amended notice with the Registrar to avoid administrative strike-off.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Directors, Officers, and Share Register Initialization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board / Cayman Islands General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt written resolutions. Appoint directors and the corporate secretary. Issue ordinary shares to subscribers and populate the register of members. File the directors’ details with the Registrar where required by law.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting or written resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar contests a director’s qualifications, replace the director by board resolution and file an amended notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption and Operational Certificate Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority / Department of Commerce and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a tax concession certificate under the Tax Concessions Act s. 6 to secure a 20-year exemption from future Cayman Islands taxes. For a pure artificial intelligence and LLM API platform, no industrial or physical operating license is required. Confirm through a written declaration that the company conducts no regulated financial business and maintains no physical premises in the Cayman Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a supplementary declaration clarifying the remote software-only nature of the business and absence of any regulated activity. Re-file after the clarification is accepted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cayman Islands Department of Commerce and Investment – no permit applicable to a remote AI/LLM API platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no industrial operating permit required for non-physical software services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cayman Islands Department of Environment / National Conservation Council
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software-only activity with no physical facilities, discharges, or emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater, VOC, or solid waste thresholds for the platform itself. If third-party data centers host compute infrastructure, those facilities are subject to the host jurisdiction’s environmental permits and ISO 14001 compliance standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a zero-footprint AI API provider. If a local office is later opened, fire safety certification from the Cayman Islands Fire Service and occupational health clearance from the Labour and Pensions Inspectorate would become mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); online portal: GOV.UK business tax services and Government Gateway (www.gov.uk/topic/business-tax; VAT registration at www.gov.uk/vat-registration; Corporation Tax at www.gov.uk/register-for-corporation-tax; MTD filings at tax.service.gov.uk). No sub-jurisdictional tax authority applies; the UK is a unitary national tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 0 — Nexus review: B2B supplies of AI/LLM API services to UK business customers fall within the UK customer's reverse charge and, absent a UK permanent establishment (PE), do not obligate the Cayman company to register with HMRC. Registration becomes compulsory when the entity has a UK PE (CTA 2009 s.19: fixed place of business, dependent agent, or UK staffed API-support/sales hub), supplies B2C digital services to UK consumers (GBP 0 registration threshold for non-established taxable persons), or imports/despatches physical goods into the UK. Step 1 — Register the non-UK (Cayman exempted) company for Corporation Tax within 3 months of commencing a UK trade via the HMRC 'non-UK company' digital route (Form CT41G); submit certified Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum & Articles, register of directors, and UK correspondence address or authorised tax agent; HMRC issues a 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). Step 2 — Register for VAT online as a non-established taxable person (Form VAT1 via Government Gateway); no statutory value threshold applies; supply Cayman legal-entity due-diligence documents, expected UK taxable turnover, banking details, and appoint a UK tax representative if HMRC requires one. Step 3 — Obtain a GB VAT registration number, an EORI number if any physical UK import/export of goods occurs, and a PAYE reference if UK employees are engaged. Step 4 — Ensure adequate Cayman economic substance (staff, premises, direction, expenditure) for intangible-property receipts to avoid the UK Offshore Receipts of Intangible Property tax (ORIP, Finance Act 2019: 20% on relevant receipts from UK payers where substance in the low-tax jurisdiction is insufficient). Step 5 — Post-registration: file Corporation Tax and VAT via Making Tax Digital-compatible software, retain records for 6 years, and manage Corporation Tax marginal bands (19% small profits rate up to GBP 50,000; 25% main rate above GBP 250,000, with associated-company rules).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Cayman domicile — no income, corporation, or withholding tax in the Cayman Islands). For UK fiscal purposes the Cayman exempted company is an opaque, non-UK-resident company taxed at entity level only on UK PE-attributable profits (Corporation Tax 19%–25%) and on UK-source intangible-property receipts under ORIP (20% where substance is inadequate); it is not a pass-through entity and no check-the-box transparency applies in the UK.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under UK law; tax residence is determined by central management and control (case law: Wood v Holden), so a Cayman board managing and controlling the company from the UK would create UK residence. Hybrid mismatch rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6A, OECD BEPS Action 2) are mandatory and carry no elective carve-out. VAT elections available to registrants: option to tax real estate, annual accounting (turnover not exceeding GBP 1.35m), cash accounting (turnover not exceeding GBP 1.35m), flat-rate scheme (turnover not exceeding GBP 150,000; narrow application to AI/data services), and margin schemes (not applicable to digital API supplies).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — UK VAT Act 1994; HMRC VAT Notice 700 series.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: UK-established persons: GBP 90,000 of taxable supplies in any rolling 12 months (effective 1 April 2024; previously GBP 85,000). Non-established taxable persons (including Cayman exempted companies): no threshold — registration is compulsory from the first UK taxable supply not already subject to the B2B reverse charge; B2C digital/e-services supplied by a non-UK supplier to UK consumers trigger VAT registration at GBP 0; UK B2B customers generally account for VAT under the reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices in the UK. Making Tax Digital for VAT (MTD) is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses: digital records must be kept and VAT Returns submitted to HMRC exclusively through MTD-compatible software via HMRC Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). Invoices may be issued in paper, PDF, or any electronic format; PEPPOL-based e-invoicing is voluntary except for certain public-sector procurement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods: 0% UK VAT (VATA 1994 s.30 and Items 1–3 Schedule 8) applies if the goods are removed from the UK by the supplier or on its behalf within 3 months of supply and within 6 months of sale/appropriation, supported by commercial evidence of export. Offshore services: B2B supplies of AI/LLM API services to customers belonging outside the UK are outside the scope of UK VAT (place of supply is the customer's country; reverse charge applies); B2C digital services to a non-UK consumer's usual residence are also outside UK VAT scope; there is no separate 'zero-rating' for services — the applicable treatment is the place-of-supply rule, evidenced by customer establishment, business status, and country records. Services physically performed wholly outside the UK (if any) may be zero-rated. The company must obtain and preserve dual evidence: (i) customer business/location evidence (VAT registration number, IP geolocation, billing address, executed contract), and (ii) for physical goods, the complete export documentation suite.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: United Kingdom Customs Export Declaration (SAD C88/EX1) transmitted via the Customs Declaration Service (CDS) with Movement Reference Number (MRN) clearance evidence
Commercial invoice (final) stating the overseas buyer, Incoterms 2020, goods/service description, value, and AI/LLM API supply characterization
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical removal from the UK (required only for export of goods; not applicable to pure digital API services)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent foreign-currency receipt record) proving payment received from the overseas customer
Customer establishment and status evidence: overseas VAT/GST registration number or non-business consumer address, IP geolocation, billing address, and bank details
Executed API service agreement / licence schedule confirming place of supply, recipient establishment, and digital-service classification
Packing list and HMRC/CDS export status message for any bonded or physical export movements (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may conduct post-clearance export audits and require production of the evidence bundle within 30 days; if zero-rating or outside-scope treatment is unsupported, HMRC issues an assessment clawing back VAT at 20% plus late-payment interest. Civil penalties: 30% (prompted disclosure) up to 100% (deliberate and concealed) of potential lost VAT under Schedule 24 Finance Act 2007; customs declaration inaccuracies attract penalties under CEMA 1979. Criminal liability: fraudulent VAT evasion and dishonest evasion (VATA 1994 s.72; FA 2000 s.144) carry penalties and imprisonment up to 7 years; HMRC may extend assessment periods to 20 years in cases of fraud (default 4 or 6 years); mutual exchange of information with overseas tax authorities applies. Note: UK VAT legislation does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline for export zero-rating; the 180-day window in this dossier is the internal compliance and evidence-repatriation benchmark.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England and HM Treasury (Exchange Control is administered on a liberalised basis under the Currency Act 1982; no separate FX control authority exists)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom maintains full capital and current account convertibility without general foreign exchange controls. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, capital repatriation, and loan repayments from UK-regulated bank accounts are generally unrestricted, subject to sanctions screening, anti-money laundering obligations, and statutory reporting under the Companies Act 2006 and the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018. A Cayman Exempted Company conducting AI/LLM API platform business through UK bank accounts may freely convert GBP to USD, EUR, or USDC via regulated payment institutions, but ensure no activity with sanctioned jurisdictions and maintain at least two weeks of source-of-funds documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies in the United Kingdom. Export receipts may be retained in any permitted currency. For statistical purposes, UK resident companies must report certain cross-border transactions through the Bank of England's International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) if the aggregate value exceeds GBP 50 million per calendar year; a Cayman exempted company without UK residence is not ordinarily a reporting entity, but the UK bank may require a self-designation form confirming non-resident status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in GBP, USD, EUR; segregated settlement sub-accounts for trade disbursement and fee collection
Global Money Account / Operational Account; eligible for multi-currency wrapper and treasury portals
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account for trade settlement and FX hedging margin posting

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for FCA-authorized E-Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, Wise, and Checkout.com; High for UK-regulated EMI/API banking fintechs accepting Cayman exempted companies under a standard non-resident corporate onboarding flow. Legal constraints: post-Brexit, UK EMIs rely on the FCA E-Money Regulations 2011 and Payment Services Regulations 2017. Circumstances around the EEA passport have ceased; a separate EEA EMI or licensed credit institution must be used for EUR-denominated SEPA pathways. Cayman companies are not automatically refused, but the EMI must verify the Cayman Islands beneficial ownership registry (Cayman DITC search) and obtain additional legal opinion if the corporate structure involves bearer shares or nominee directors. Do not rely on unregulated crypto-only 'EMI' platforms; any USDC/Stablecoin settlement must be executed via an FCA-registered crypto asset business under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 (cryptoasset AML/CTF regime) with the EMI as the bridge to fiat rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For UK high-street banks, physical presence of all directors is not strictly mandated. Most tier-1 banks accept a fully remote onboarding with: (i) digital identity verification using UK/EU/Cayman passports, (ii) a live video call with the compliance officer (director(s) must appear), and (iii) submission of notarised or apostilled corporate documents from the Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies. The Cayman exempted company need not maintain a UK physical office; a registered office in the Cayman Islands and a UK professional introduction, such as a corporate service provider or a UK-regulated law firm, materially increases approval probability. Some regional UK banks, including Lloyds and NatWest, may demand one director to attend a physical interview at a London branch if the corporate ownership is deemed opaque or the revenue model shows a material crypto-asset component.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Islands domicile flagged as high-risk tax haven and perceived as opaque ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation from Cayman Registrar; Certificate of Good Standing; registered agent letter; full ultimate beneficial ownership register; corporate organisational chart; directors' and shareholders' register; notarised passport copies; recent utility bill or bank reference; legal opinion from a recognised UK law firm opining on creditworthiness and tax transparency under CRS reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model incorporates cryptocurrency / USDC settlement rails, triggering enhanced due diligence even though AI API platform risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FCA registration or MLR registration confirmation for the crypto-asset component; written business description with customer-facing API terms; transaction volume forecast; AML policies and procedures of the entity; wallet ownership and custody documentation; third-party audit report of the smart contract or treasury policies; evidence that USDC conversion is executed through a UK-regulated digital asset firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No historical trading record or inactive shell company status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising account opening; draft or executed API platform contracts with commercial counterparties; proof of domain / intellectual property ownership; capital injection plan with source-of-funds proof; audited or management accounts; bank reference from the Cayman Islands private bank; shareholder commitment letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected cross-border wire volumes with AI API billing to diverse geographies, potentially triggering sanctions screening false positives
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer KYC pack from the platform itself; geolocation of end-users; export-control compliance policies; contractual clauses prohibiting use in sanctioned jurisdictions; IP-blocking evidence; periodic transaction monitoring report prepared by a compliance consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection to the UK operating account from Cayman shareholders should be effected via SWIFT MT103 from the Cayman corporate bank or a licensed corporate service provider. The transfer reference must include the invoice or capital contribution purpose, e.g.,
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for software licensing, cloud compute, and LLM API vendor payments should be executed by MT103 across CHAPS (GBP domestically), TARGET2 (EUR via an EU correspondent), or via FEDWIRE / CHIPS for USD. For major infrastructure vendors (AWS, Microsoft Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic), US USD accounts are most efficient. Commercial Letters of Credit are not typical for AI API platform disbursements but may be used only for fixed-capacity GPU hosting agreements where the supplier demands payment security; otherwise standard MT103 with 48-hour settlement is the freight-free treasury rail. Consider a UK EMI with direct SEPA instant for EUR vendor payments to reduce correspondent banking costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Swaps / Prime of Prime facilities via UK banks
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible emerging-market exposure (permitted under UK law, subject to FCA prudential and EMIR reporting)
Deliverable forwards in G10 currencies, including GBP/USD, EUR/USD, GBP/EUR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and annual company licence fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each year during January; the statutory annual return and fee are generally required by 31 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fees apply under the prescribed Companies Registry tariff. Continued non-payment may result in the company being struck off the register after the statutory default and notice process, with restoration costs and possible loss of limited-liability protection during strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority through the Department for International Tax Cooperation portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within 12 months after the end of each financial year, where applicable. A notification is required even where the entity claims that no relevant activity is conducted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties may apply for failure to notify or inaccurate information. Failure to satisfy applicable economic-substance requirements may trigger additional penalties, information exchange, and enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory independent-audit requirement applies to an ordinary Cayman exempted company conducting non-regulated business. An audit may be required by sector-specific legislation, a regulatory licence, constitutional documents, financing terms, or investor requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No single mandatory accounting framework applies to an ordinary exempted company. IFRS or consistently applied US GAAP is commonly used; regulated entities must follow the framework prescribed by the applicable Cayman regulator.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate beneficial-ownership information and provide it through its corporate services provider or the prescribed reporting mechanism. Ownership, control, and shareholder-transfer changes must be reviewed annually and reported or updated promptly within the applicable statutory period, generally within 30 days. There is no public beneficial-ownership register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners or prescribed beneficial-ownership records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-8,000 per year; zero where no audit is legally or contractually required, and approximately 3,000-8,000 for a small non-regulated company if an audit is commissioned
